cockroachdb: ships upstream's OWN official per-arch self-contained binary tarball
(sha256-verified against binaries.cockroachdb.com's published .sha256sum), hardened
on a minimal apko base. Single version: the newest stable patch, full X.Y.Z, used
as-is.
  __VER__     = version (rendered quoted into melange version:)
  __SHA_AMD__ = linux-amd64 tarball sha256   __SHA_ARM__ = linux-arm64 tarball sha256

FROZEN 2026-10-14 (user decision): keep the published 2.9.7, take NO further updates.
  On 2026-10-09 Deno announced its team is joining Cloudflare: Deno Deploy shuts down about six
  months later, and the runtime gets one more year of monthly bug-fix and security releases, then
  its own development ends (no successor maintainer named). scripts/check/deno.py caps candidates
  at 2.9.7 so the daily update check never offers a bump. Sources:
  https://alternativeto.net/news/2026/10/deno-team-joins-cloudflare-as-runtime-development-winds-down/
  https://www.beri.net/article/cloudflare-deno-acquisition-deno-deploy-shutdown-six-months-runtime-one-year-workers-migration
  https://www.highcircl.com/en/blog/deno-joins-cloudflare-runtime-end (2026-10-10; counts both clocks
  from 2026-10-09: Deploy off around April 2027, runtime development ends around October 2027; neither
  date is official, and Deno says the code stays open source for anyone who continues it.)
  The 2026-10-13 hold below still describes the 7 hidden crate findings in 2.9.7.
STATUS: BLOCKED 2026-10-13 on deno's own Cargo.lock. The release binary carries no
cargo-auditable data (no .dep-v0 section), so Trivy never saw its crates and the
published 2.9.7 passed the gate blind. The v2.9.7 Cargo.lock, scanned with the gate's
flags, holds 7 fixable findings, and the crate-version strings inside the binary
confirm all 7 ship:
  hickory-resolver 0.25.2  GHSA-5j98-2g5x-46v6 HIGH, GHSA-6f2x-v7q7-m7m5 MEDIUM  (fix 0.26.2)
  hickory-proto 0.25.2     GHSA-q2qq-hmj6-3wpp MEDIUM                            (fix 0.26.1)
  rustls 0.23.40           GHSA-2mjx-qc3c-rqvc MEDIUM                            (fix 0.23.45)
  rand 0.8.5, 0.9.2        GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc LOW                               (fix 0.8.6/0.9.3)
  xxhash-rust 0.8.15       GHSA-6g2r-675j-hx59 LOW                               (fix 0.8.16)
Not a VEX: only three are provably absent. cargo tree on v2.9.7 resolves hickory-resolver
to [default,serde,system-config,tokio] with no __dnssec feature, so hickory-resolver-0.25.2
src/resolver.rs:91-104 never builds the DnssecDnsHandle (GHSA-5j98); rand has no `log`
feature and xxhash-rust only `xxh64`. The CNAME and name-compression bugs (Deno.resolveDns,
ext/net/ops.rs:1187-1191) and the rustls one (every fetch and TLS connection) are
reachable in a general runtime.
Not a source build: hickory 0.25 to 0.26 is a breaking API change (deno PR #36322, open
and conflicting), so a cargo update cannot take it.
UNBLOCK when a deno release pins hickory-resolver >= 0.26.2, hickory-proto >= 0.26.1 and
rustls >= 0.23.45 (main still had 0.25.2 and 0.23.40 on 2026-10-13): add the version with
its zip and Cargo.lock sha256s, set BLOCKED=0, dispatch. The recipe installs that
Cargo.lock in the image, so the gate scans every crate; VEX what is left only with the
feature evidence above.

Measured: run 38373558044 built 0.9.1 with cargo auditable on both arches; the gate now sees
the binary crates and its ONLY finding is thrift 0.17.0 (rustls floored to 0.23.45; rustls-webpki

parquet and quickwit to move. The published 0.9.1 predates auditable and is blind to this.

thrift ships a 0.17.x fix: set BLOCKED=0, bump VERSIONS, dispatch; recipe is ready.
